name: Kubernetes Deployment Agent
description: Reads YAML manifests, validates them against Kubernetes best practices (resource limits, liveness probes, security contexts), generates Helm charts, runs dry-run deployments across multiple environments (dev, staging, prod), and supports rollback on failure.

manifest-validation.description: Validates Kubernetes YAML manifests against best practices including resource limits, liveness/readiness probes, and security contexts

tests.description: Identifies containers missing CPU/memory resource limits and requests
tests.prompt:
Validate this Kubernetes deployment manifest:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: web-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: web-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: web-app
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: web-app
        image: nginx:1.25
        ports:
        - containerPort: 80
```

tests.description: Flags missing liveness and readiness probes
tests.prompt:
Check this deployment for best practice violations:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: api-server
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: api-server
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: api-server
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: api
        image: myregistry/api:v2.1
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 256Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 250m
            memory: 128Mi
```

tests.description: Warns about missing security contexts and running as root
tests.prompt:
Audit this manifest for security issues:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: payment-service
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: payment
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: payment
        image: myregistry/payment:v1.0
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8443
```

tests.description: Approves a well-configured manifest with all best practices
tests.prompt:
Validate this deployment manifest:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: secure-app
spec:
  replicas: 3
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: secure-app
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: secure-app
    spec:
      securityContext:
        runAsNonRoot: true
        fsGroup: 1000
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: myregistry/app:v3.2@sha256:abc123
        ports:
        - containerPort: 8080
        resources:
          limits:
            cpu: 1000m
            memory: 512Mi
          requests:
            cpu: 500m
            memory: 256Mi
        livenessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /healthz
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 15
          periodSeconds: 10
        readinessProbe:
          httpGet:
            path: /ready
            port: 8080
          initialDelaySeconds: 5
          periodSeconds: 5
        securityContext:
          allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
          readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
```

helm-chart-generation.description: Generates Helm charts from raw Kubernetes manifests with parameterized values for multi-environment support

tests.description: Generates a valid Chart.yaml with proper metadata
tests.prompt: Generate a Helm chart for a web application called 'order-service' version 2.1.0. Include the Chart.yaml content.

tests.description: Creates a values.yaml with environment-parameterized settings
tests.prompt: Generate a Helm values.yaml for a microservice that needs to support dev (1 replica, 256Mi memory), staging (2 replicas, 512Mi memory), and prod (3 replicas, 1Gi memory) environments. Show the default values.yaml.

tests.description: Converts a raw deployment manifest into a Helm template with proper Go template syntax
tests.prompt:
Convert this raw Kubernetes deployment to a Helm template:
```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: user-service
spec:
  replicas: 3
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: user-service
        image: myregistry/user-service:v1.5
        resources:
          limits:
            memory: 512Mi
```

multi-environment-support.description: Manages deployments across dev, staging, and prod environments with appropriate configurations and safeguards

tests.description: Produces correct configuration differences per environment
tests.prompt: I need to deploy the notification-service to all three environments. Dev should use 1 replica with debug logging, staging should use 2 replicas with info logging, and prod should use 5 replicas with warn logging and PodDisruptionBudget. What are the environment-specific configurations?

tests.description: Applies additional safeguards for production deployments
tests.prompt: What safeguards should be applied when deploying to production versus dev for a critical payment service?

tests.description: Ensures proper namespace usage per environment
tests.prompt: Set up the namespace and context configuration for deploying analytics-service across dev, staging, and prod environments.

dry-run-deployment.description: Executes dry-run deployments to validate manifests will apply correctly without making actual changes

tests.description: Generates correct kubectl or helm dry-run commands
tests.prompt: Run a dry-run deployment of the order-service Helm chart to the staging namespace. Show the exact commands.

tests.description: Issues a shell execution tool call for the dry-run
tests.prompt: Execute a dry-run deployment for the auth-service to the dev environment using helm upgrade --install with --dry-run flag.

tests.description: Correctly interprets and explains dry-run errors
tests.prompt:
The dry-run returned this error:
```
Error: UPGRADE FAILED: cannot patch "cache-service" with kind Deployment: Deployment.apps "cache-service" is invalid: spec.selector: Invalid value: v1.LabelSelector{MatchLabels:map[string]string{"app":"cache-v2"}, MatchExpressions:[]v1.LabelSelectorRequirement(nil)}: field is immutable
```
What went wrong and how do I fix it?

rollback-on-failure.description: Detects deployment failures and executes rollback procedures to restore the previous stable state

tests.description: Generates correct rollback commands for both kubectl and helm
tests.prompt: The deployment of payment-service v2.3.0 to production failed. The pods are in CrashLoopBackOff. How do I rollback?

tests.description: Proposes a complete rollback strategy including verification steps
tests.prompt: Design a rollback procedure for a failed production deployment of order-service. Include detection, rollback execution, and post-rollback verification.

tests.description: Configures automatic rollback mechanisms in Helm or deployment spec
tests.prompt: How do I configure automatic rollback on failure for Helm deployments? Show the configuration.
